title: Extend autoresearch to support multi-GPU runs with gradient synchronization
description:
Currently autoresearch runs on a single GPU. Some users have machines with 2–4 GPUs and want to use them all. Add multi-GPU support using PyTorch DDP (DistributedDataParallel) while preserving everything that makes autoresearch work: the 5-minute budget, the val_bpb metric, git-based experiment tracking.

Key requirements:
  - Auto-detect number of available GPUs. If only 1 GPU, run as before (no DDP overhead).
  - If >1 GPU, launch training with torchrun (DDP). The existing `uv run train.py` invocation must still work; internally it should re-launch itself under torchrun if needed.
  - Effective batch size scales with number of GPUs (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE splits across GPUs)
  - The 5-minute budget is wall-clock time on rank 0 (same as single-GPU)
  - val_bpb evaluation runs only on rank 0 after barrier sync
  - Only rank 0 writes to results.tsv and run.log
  - peak_vram_mb reported is the max across all ranks
  - The MuonAdamW optimizer must work correctly under DDP (Muon requires all-reduce for gradient orthogonalization)
  - All existing single-GPU tests must pass when CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES limits to 1 GPU

Do NOT add any new dependencies. Use only torch.distributed which is already available via the PyTorch install.
acceptance_criteria: With 1 GPU (or CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0), training behavior is identical to baseline
With 2+ GPUs, training launches via DDP automatically
uv run train.py works as the sole entry point (no separate launch command needed)
Effective batch size is TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE regardless of GPU count
val_bpb is evaluated only on rank 0 after all ranks sync
Only rank 0 writes to run.log and results.tsv
peak_vram_mb is the max across all ranks
MuonAdamW Nesterov update uses properly all-reduced gradients
5-minute budget is enforced on wall clock (rank 0 clock)
All single-GPU tests pass with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set to one device
